verdict_reason: The promoted scaling-region kernel IS a faithful Grassberger-Procaccia estimator: on a fresh RK4 Lorenz attractor (2000 sampled states of the 3-D state space) it returns D2 = 2.0405 at R^2 = 0.9995 against GP 1983's published 2.05 +- 0.01, a relative error of -0.46%, and on uniform d-cubes at N=2000 it reads 1.9803 / 2.8908 / 4.7080 / 7.0580 for d = 2 / 3 / 5 / 8 (-1.0% to -11.8%, biased low as under-resolution predicts). Two caveats keep it off GREEN, both established below with numbers: the headline is the exponent of the CONTINUOUS part rather than strict GP (C(r) drops the coincident pairs), and the entire atomic-measure branch is provably dead code.
comparable_reason: D2 is dimensionless and bounded by the intrinsic dimension of the cloud, not by d_model, so it is not a width proxy. It IS a point-count proxy in the under-resolved regime: the shipped default gives only N=100 mean-pooled points, gpt2 reports correlation_dimension 5.410815215459207 with _meta_correlation_dimension_eckmann_ruelle_slope_bound 4.0 and _meta_correlation_dimension_under_resolved True, i.e. the reported value exceeds its own resolution bound. Comparisons are valid only between models measured at the same N.
github_reason: Grassberger & Procaccia 1983 released no code. I read the installed nolds 0.6.3 corr_dim source to settle the open question about the >0 filter: nolds forms C(r) = (1/(n(n-1))) * sum(dists <= r) over ALL off-diagonal pairs, so coincident pairs (distance 0 <= r) ARE counted and DO create the atom floor. BLME fits on distances[distances > 0] and therefore computes a different estimand whenever any pair coincides. nolds' scalar D2 is not directly comparable head-to-head because it delay-embeds a scalar series rather than taking a point cloud, so this is PARTIAL, not YES.
paper_reason: Grassberger & Procaccia 1983 (PRL 50, 346) publish D2 = 2.05 +- 0.01 for the Lorenz attractor. Integrating the Lorenz system with RK4 (dt=0.01, sigma=10, rho=28, beta=8/3, 20000-step transient discarded), sampling 2000 states and running BLME's promoted scaling-region kernel on the 3-D state space gives 2.0405 at R^2 = 0.9995 -- relative error 0.46%, inside their stated uncertainty band. The DEMOTED percentile-window kernel gives 1.4739 on the identical distances, -28.10%, confirming that the promotion of the scaling-region window was the right call.
confounds_reason: Not a width or vocabulary proxy -- D2 is bounded by the manifold dimension, not d_model. It is a sample-size proxy in the regime the defaults put it in: the Eckmann-Ruelle bound at N=100 is 4.0 and gpt2 reports 5.41, so what is being read is partly the resolution ceiling of 4950 pairs rather than the geometry. Per the campaign brief I do NOT re-file the Eckmann-Ruelle gating itself; I record it only as the reason comparability is conditional on matched N.
